Uses gamma minus one rather than gamma itself
Assumes a linear rather than inverse-square or exponential relation

questions.hint: Invert gamma = 1/sqrt(1 minus beta squared) rather than using the raw ratio.

questions.stem: During a worked example, muons have proper lifetime 3.00 microseconds; observers clock one at 7.52 × 10^0 microseconds. What is its speed as a fraction of c?

options.misconception: Confuses the moving-frame value with the proper-frame value
Uses gamma minus one rather than gamma itself
Assumes a linear rather than inverse-square or exponential relation

questions.explanation: From time dilation, tobs = gamma times t0, so gamma = tobs/t0 and beta = sqrt(1 - 1/gamma^2) = sqrt(1 - (t0/tobs)^2) = 0.917. The ratio t0/tobs equals 1/gamma, not beta; gamma minus one and beta squared are unrelated to the recovered speed. The particle therefore moves at about 0.917c.
questions.hint: Invert gamma = 1/sqrt(1 minus beta squared) rather than using the raw ratio.

questions.stem: A muon with proper lifetime 1.00 microseconds travels at 0.300c. How far does it travel in the laboratory before decaying?

Halves the distance without a physical basis
